shared_foundation.name: Shared Foundation & Types
shared_foundation.description: Shared TypeScript types, utility functions, database/Redis client abstractions, and testing helpers used across all services. Includes: UUID generation, ISO 8601 date helpers, bitmask utilities, SHA-256 hashing for content-addressable IDs, HTTP client wrapper for inter-service calls, configuration management (env vars for service URLs, DB connection strings, Redis URLs), placeholder auth middleware, common error response shapes, and mock/in-memory substitutes for PostgreSQL, Redis, and Kafka used in tests. This is the only component that other services import from directly.

shared_types.name: Shared Type Definitions
shared_types.description: TypeScript type/interface definitions for all cross-service contracts: UUIDs, date ranges, API response envelopes, error shapes, entity IDs (unit_id, property_id, brand_id, booking_id, event_id, payout_id), bitmask type aliases, pricing structs, booking status enums, event payload schemas, and 4-tier settings types. These types are the single source of truth for API contract shapes between services.

shared_db_client.name: PostgreSQL Client Abstraction
shared_db_client.description: A thin wrapper around a PostgreSQL driver (deno-postgres) providing typed query execution, connection pooling config, schema-per-service namespace isolation, and migration runner. Exposes a factory function that takes a schema name and returns a scoped client. Includes an in-memory mock implementation for testing that supports basic SQL-like operations.

shared_redis_client.name: Redis Client Abstraction
shared_redis_client.description: A thin wrapper around a Redis driver providing typed get/set/delete, key prefix namespacing per service, TTL management, and bitmask-specific operations (SETBIT, GETBIT, BITCOUNT, BITOP). Includes an in-memory mock implementation for testing.

shared_test_helpers.name: Test Helpers & Mocks
shared_test_helpers.description: Shared testing utilities: factory functions for creating test entities (units, properties, bookings, events), HTTP request/response test helpers for contract testing, assertion helpers for API response shapes, mock Kafka producer/consumer, and test fixture data from reference/test_examples/. All mocks operate in-memory with no external service dependencies.

shared_config.name: Configuration & Service Discovery
shared_config.description: Centralized configuration loading from environment variables. Provides typed config objects for each service including: service URLs (for inter-service HTTP calls), database connection strings, Redis URLs, port assignments, and feature flags. Defaults to localhost for development.

shared_http_client.name: Inter-Service HTTP Client
shared_http_client.description: A typed HTTP client wrapper for service-to-service communication. Handles JSON serialization/deserialization, timeout configuration, retry with backoff, circuit breaker pattern for resilience, and standardized error propagation. Each service uses this to call other services rather than raw fetch.

availability_service.name: Availability Service
availability_service.description: Bitmask-based availability cache providing O(1) date range availability checks for rental units. Stores availability as bitmasks in Redis (one bit per day, 365+ days per unit). Provides endpoints to check availability for a date range, update availability (block/unblock dates), and bulk-query multiple units. PostgreSQL stores the authoritative availability records; Redis bitmasks are the hot cache. This is the most latency-critical service in the checkout flow.

availability_schema.name: Availability Database Schema & Repository
availability_schema.description: PostgreSQL schema definition and data access layer for the availability service. Tables: availability_blocks (unit_id, start_date, end_date, block_type, source), availability_cache_metadata (unit_id, cache_epoch, last_synced). Repository functions for CRUD operations on availability blocks, cache invalidation tracking, and bitmask rebuild queries.

availability_bitmask_engine.name: Bitmask Engine
availability_bitmask_engine.description: Core bitmask logic for O(1) availability checks. Functions: buildBitmask(blocks, epoch) → Uint8Array, checkRange(bitmask, startDay, endDay) → boolean, setRange(bitmask, startDay, endDay, available) → Uint8Array, bitmaskToRedisKey(unitId, epoch) → string. Uses a fixed epoch (e.g., 2024-01-01) and maps calendar dates to bit offsets. Handles Redis read/write of bitmasks, cache warming on startup, and cache invalidation on updates.

availability_api.name: Availability API Endpoints
availability_api.description: Oak HTTP router implementing availability endpoints: GET /availability/:unit_id?start=&end= (check availability, returns boolean + blocked dates), POST /availability/:unit_id/block (block date range), DELETE /availability/:unit_id/block (unblock date range), GET /availability/bulk?unit_ids=&start=&end= (multi-unit check). All responses follow shared API envelope. Validates inputs, delegates to bitmask engine, falls back to DB on cache miss.

availability_tests.name: Availability Service Tests
availability_tests.description: Test suite for the availability service: unit tests for bitmask operations (edge cases: month boundaries, leap years, single-day ranges, full-year ranges), repository tests with mock DB, API contract tests validating request/response shapes against the architecture spec, integration tests for cache-miss-to-DB fallback, and performance assertions that bitmask checks complete in <1ms.

pricing_service.name: Pricing Service
pricing_service.description: Rate cache service providing fast price lookups for rental units. Stores nightly rates hash-sharded by unit_id in Redis for O(1) lookups. Supports dynamic pricing with date-specific rates, seasonal rates, length-of-stay discounts, and fees/taxes computation. PostgreSQL stores authoritative rate configurations; Redis is the hot cache sharded by unit_id hash for even distribution.

contract.name: Pricing Service
contract.description: Rate cache service providing fast price lookups for rental units. Stores nightly rates hash-sharded by unit_id in Redis for O(1) lookups. Supports dynamic pricing with date-specific rates, seasonal rates, length-of-stay discounts, and fees/taxes computation. PostgreSQL stores authoritative rate configurations; Redis is the hot cache sharded by unit_id hash for even distribution. Thin orchestration facade exposing 7 public functions via a factory-created PricingService object: getQuote (cache-aside + full computation pipeline), getRates (cache-aside nightly rate lookup), updateRateConfiguration (write-through + cache invalidation), upsertFee (write-through + cache invalidation), warmCache (bulk cache population), invalidateCache (explicit cache bust), plus the createPricingService factory. Cache strategy is cache-aside reads with write-through invalidation and graceful degradation (Redis failure → DB fallback, never an error to callers). The computation pipeline follows strict order: nightly rates → subtotal → LOS discount → flat fees → percentage fees → taxes → grand total. All arithmetic in CentsAmount (integer cents), bankers rounding for percentage calculations. File organization: mod.ts (public exports, <300 lines), types.ts (all contract types), service.ts (orchestration implementation), pipeline.ts (quote computation pipeline), deps.ts (dependency interface definitions).

functions.name: getQuote
functions.description: Computes a full price breakdown for a potential stay. Implements cache-aside pattern: checks Redis cache first for nightly rates, falls back to PostgreSQL via pricing_schema.resolveRatesForDateRange on miss, populates cache on miss. Then runs the computation pipeline in strict order: (1) resolve nightly rates from cache/DB, (2) sum to nightlySubtotal, (3) apply best LOS discount → discountedSubtotal, (4) add flat fees, (5) add percentage fees on discountedSubtotal → feesTotal, (6) compute taxes on (discountedSubtotal + taxable fees) → taxesTotal, (7) grandTotal = discountedSubtotal + feesTotal + taxesTotal. Each step produces typed line items for full transparency. All arithmetic in integer cents with bankers rounding. Redis failures are silently logged and result in DB fallback — never an error to callers.

Delegates to pricing_schema for PostgreSQL persistence (updateRatePlan), then invalidates the Redis cache for the unit via pricing_cache_engine.invalidateUnit. The cache invalidation happens after the DB commit to ensure consistency. If cache invalidation fails, the DB update is still committed (cache will eventually expire or be warmed). Returns the updated configuration summary.

functions.name: warmCache
functions.description: Bulk cache population for a list of units over a date range. For each unit, resolves rates from PostgreSQL via pricing_schema.resolveRatesForDateRange and writes them to Redis via pricing_cache_engine.cacheRates. Processes units in batches (configurable via CacheConfig.warmBatchSize) for controlled concurrency. Individual unit failures do not abort the batch — each unit's result is reported independently. This is a best-effort operation designed for pre-warming before high-traffic periods.

preconditions: unitIds is non-empty and contains at most 10000 entries
dateRange.startDate < dateRange.endDate

All unit IDs are valid UUID v4 strings

functions.name: invalidateCache
functions.description: Explicitly invalidates (deletes) the Redis cache for a specific unit. Delegates to pricing_cache_engine.invalidateUnit. Idempotent — succeeds even if the cache key does not exist. Redis failures are caught and reported in the result (success=false) but never thrown.

error_cases.condition: unitId is not a valid UUID v4 string

postconditions: On success, value is an InvalidateResult
If Redis was reachable, the cache key for the unit no longer exists
success is true if Redis DEL succeeded or key did not exist, false if Redis was unreachable

This function never returns a ServiceResultErr — Redis failures are reported via InvalidateResult.success=false

invariants: All monetary values (rates, fees, taxes, subtotals, totals, discounts) are represented as non-negative integers in minor currency units (CentsAmount). No floating-point arithmetic is ever used for money.
All date ranges use half-open intervals [start, end) where start < end. A stay of N nights has checkIn and checkOut exactly N days apart.
Currency codes are ISO 4217 three-letter uppercase codes. All monetary entities within a single quote/rate lookup share the same currency. Cross-currency mixing within a single operation is an error.

The computation pipeline order is fixed and immutable: (1) resolve nightly rates, (2) sum to nightlySubtotal, (3) apply single best LOS discount → discountedSubtotal, (4) add flat fees, (5) add percentage fees on discountedSubtotal, (6) compute taxes on (discountedSubtotal + taxable fees), (7) grandTotal = discountedSubtotal + feesTotal + taxesTotal.

Only the single best (highest discount percentage) active LOS discount where minNights <= numNights is applied. If no LOS discount qualifies, no discount is applied and discountedSubtotal equals nightlySubtotal.
Percentage fees and tax rates are stored in basis points (0-10000 where 10000 = 100%). Integer division uses banker's rounding (round half to even).
Taxes are computed on (discountedSubtotal + sum of taxable fee amounts). Non-taxable fees are excluded from the tax base.
No public method of the PricingService ever throws an exception. All operations return ServiceResult (discriminated union: ok with value, or err with PricingServiceError).

Cache failures (Redis unavailable, timeout, deserialization error) are always silent to callers. The service falls back to PostgreSQL on any cache failure and logs the error. Cache failures never produce a ServiceResultErr.

Write-through cache invalidation occurs after PostgreSQL commit on all mutation operations (updateRateConfiguration, upsertFee). If cache invalidation fails, the DB mutation is NOT rolled back — cache will eventually expire via TTL.

The Redis cache is hash-sharded by unit_id using consistent hashing (CRC32 or equivalent). The shard key format is 'pricing:{N}:{unit_id}' where N = hash(unit_id) % shard_count. Same unit_id always maps to the same shard.

Cache-aside read pattern: check Redis → on miss, read from PostgreSQL → populate Redis (fire-and-forget). Cache reads require ALL dates in range to be present and valid; partial hits are treated as full misses.

The PricingService facade is stateless and safe for concurrent use. All state resides in PostgreSQL (authoritative) and Redis (cache). Multiple PricingService instances sharing the same pool and Redis client are safe.
Dependency errors from pricing_schema and pricing_cache_engine are wrapped into PricingServiceError with appropriate kind values. Internal error types are never leaked to callers.

QuoteBreakdown line item sums are exact: nightlySubtotal == sum(nightlyRates[].rate), feesTotal == sum(fees[].resolvedAmount), taxesTotal == sum(taxes[].taxAmount), grandTotal == discountedSubtotal + feesTotal + taxesTotal. No rounding drift is permitted.
requires: pricing_schema must be initialized with a connected PostgreSQL pool and the pricing schema migration must have been run
pricing_cache_engine must be constructable with a Redis client (connection may be down — graceful degradation applies)
All five pricing schema tables (rate_plans, rate_overrides, fees, taxes, los_discounts) must exist in the PostgreSQL pricing namespace
The btree_gist extension must be enabled in PostgreSQL for EXCLUDE constraints on rate_overrides

pricing_schema.name: Pricing Database Schema & Repository
pricing_schema.description: PostgreSQL schema and data access layer for pricing. Tables: rate_plans (unit_id, name, base_rate, currency), rate_overrides (rate_plan_id, date_start, date_end, nightly_rate), fees (unit_id, fee_type, amount, is_percentage), taxes (unit_id, tax_type, rate), los_discounts (unit_id, min_nights, discount_pct). Repository functions for rate resolution given a unit and date range.

pricing_cache_engine.name: Hash-Sharded Price Cache
pricing_cache_engine.description: Redis caching layer for pricing data, hash-sharded by unit_id. Functions: shardKey(unitId) → Redis key using consistent hash, cacheRates(unitId, rates) → void, getCachedRates(unitId, dateRange) → rates|null, invalidateUnit(unitId) → void. Implements cache-aside pattern: check Redis first, fall back to DB, populate cache on miss. Shard count configurable via env var.

pricing_api.name: Pricing API Endpoints
pricing_api.description: Oak HTTP router implementing pricing endpoints: GET /pricing/:unit_id/quote?start=&end=&guests= (compute total price breakdown: nightly rates, fees, taxes, discounts, total), GET /pricing/:unit_id/rates?start=&end= (raw nightly rates), PUT /pricing/:unit_id/rates (update rate configuration), POST /pricing/:unit_id/fees (add/update fees). Returns structured price breakdowns with currency and all line items.

pricing_tests.name: Pricing Service Tests
pricing_tests.description: Test suite for pricing: unit tests for rate calculation logic (seasonal overlaps, LOS discounts, fee/tax stacking), cache shard distribution tests, API contract tests, tests for cache miss/hit paths, and edge cases (zero-night stays, currency rounding, overlapping rate overrides).

contract.name: Pricing Service Tests
contract.description: Test suite for the rate cache pricing service. Covers unit tests for rate calculation logic (seasonal overlaps, LOS discounts, fee/tax stacking), cache shard distribution tests, API contract tests, cache miss/hit path tests, serialization round-trip tests, and edge cases (zero-night stays, currency rounding, overlapping rate overrides). All monetary values use integer minor-unit (cents) arithmetic. The computation pipeline order is codified as: base rates → seasonal/override resolution → LOS discount → flat fees → percentage fees → taxes. Each pipeline step is a pure function, independently testable. Tests use Deno BDD style with injected mock RedisClient and RateRepository interfaces.

invariants: All monetary amounts are represented as non-negative integers in minor currency units (cents). No floating-point money arithmetic is ever used.
CurrencyCode is always an uppercase ISO 4217 three-letter string (e.g. 'USD', 'EUR').

All date values (ISODateString) conform to ISO 8601 UTC format YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ.
The calculation pipeline is always applied in strict order: base rates → seasonal/override resolution → LOS discount → flat fees → percentage fees → taxes.
Shard assignment is deterministic: the same UnitId always maps to the same shard index for a given shard count.
Result types always contain exactly one of 'ok' value or 'error' value, never both and never neither.
Test fixture factories always produce valid domain objects with all required fields populated by sensible defaults.
Mock call counters are monotonically non-decreasing integers starting at zero.
PriceBreakdown line items sum exactly to the total field — no rounding drift is permitted.

property_service.name: Property Service
property_service.description: Property and unit management with a 4-tier settings override hierarchy (platform → brand → property → unit). Manages the entity hierarchy: platforms contain brands, brands contain properties, properties contain units. Settings at any tier can be overridden by more specific tiers using most-specific-wins with deep merge semantics. This is the source of truth for property/unit metadata consumed by other services.

property_schema.name: Property Database Schema & Repository
property_schema.description: PostgreSQL schema and data access layer for the property hierarchy. Tables: platforms (id, name, settings JSONB), brands (id, platform_id, name, settings JSONB), properties (id, brand_id, name, address, settings JSONB), units (id, property_id, name, type, bedrooms, bathrooms, max_guests, settings JSONB). Repository functions for full CRUD on each entity level, with eager loading of the hierarchy chain for settings resolution.

property_override_engine.name: 4-Tier Override Engine
property_override_engine.description: Settings resolution engine implementing the 4-tier override hierarchy. Given a unit_id, loads settings from all 4 tiers (platform → brand → property → unit) and produces a merged settings object using most-specific-wins semantics with deep merge on nested objects. Functions: resolveSettings(unitId) → mergedSettings, resolveSettingsAtTier(entityId, tier) → partialSettings. Caches resolved settings in Redis with invalidation on any tier update.

property_api.name: Property API Endpoints
property_api.description: Oak HTTP router implementing property management endpoints: CRUD for platforms, brands, properties, units (standard REST). GET /units/:unit_id/settings (resolved merged settings), PUT /units/:unit_id/settings (update unit-level settings), GET /properties/:property_id/units (list units), GET /units/:unit_id (full unit details with resolved settings). Search/filter endpoints for units by location, capacity, amenities.

property_tests.name: Property Service Tests
property_tests.description: Test suite for property service: unit tests for deep merge logic (nested objects, array handling, null overrides), override hierarchy resolution tests (all 4 tiers, partial overrides, missing tiers), CRUD API contract tests, cache invalidation tests (updating brand settings invalidates all child unit caches), and edge cases (orphaned entities, circular references prevention).

event_service.name: Event Service
event_service.description: Kafka-based event bus providing content-addressable event storage and pub/sub for all inter-service events. Events are identified by SHA-256 hash of (payload + timestamp + source) ensuring uniqueness and enabling deduplication. Provides HTTP endpoints for publishing and subscribing to events, backed by Kafka for durability and PostgreSQL for event log persistence. Other services emit events here for audit trail and async processing.

event_schema.name: Event Database Schema & Repository
event_schema.description: PostgreSQL schema and data access layer for events. Tables: events (event_id SHA-256 hash as PK, topic, source_service, payload JSONB, created_at, version), event_subscriptions (subscriber_id, topic_pattern, callback_url, active). Repository functions for event storage (idempotent upsert by content-addressable ID), querying by topic/time range/source, and subscription management.

event_content_addressing.name: Content-Addressable Event Engine
event_content_addressing.description: Core event processing logic. Functions: computeEventId(payload, timestamp, source) → SHA-256 hex string, publishEvent(topic, payload, source) → eventId (computes ID, stores in DB, publishes to Kafka topic), consumeEvents(topic, handler) → subscription, replayEvents(topic, since) → event stream. Includes mock Kafka producer/consumer that uses in-memory queues for testing. Handles deduplication via content-addressable IDs.

event_api.name: Event API Endpoints
event_api.description: Oak HTTP router implementing event endpoints: POST /events (publish event with topic + payload, returns event_id), GET /events/:event_id (retrieve event by content-addressable ID), GET /events?topic=&since=&until= (query events by topic and time range), POST /subscriptions (register webhook callback for topic), DELETE /subscriptions/:id (remove subscription). Supports both push (webhook) and pull (polling) consumption patterns.

event_tests.name: Event Service Tests
event_tests.description: Test suite for event service: unit tests for SHA-256 content addressing (deterministic IDs, timestamp inclusion prevents collisions on identical payloads), idempotent publish tests (same event twice = one stored record), API contract tests, subscription/webhook delivery tests with mock HTTP, event replay ordering tests, and Kafka mock integration tests.

sync_service.name: Sync Service
sync_service.description: Bidirectional PMS (Property Management System) synchronization with 8 stub adapters. Pulls availability, rates, and bookings from external PMS systems and pushes Wander state changes back. Each adapter implements a common interface; actual implementations are stubs/mocks simulating real PMS APIs. Manages sync state, conflict resolution, and rate limiting per PMS.

sync_adapter_interface.name: PMS Adapter Interface & Stub Implementations
sync_adapter_interface.description: Defines the common adapter interface: pullAvailability(unitMapping) → blocks[], pullRates(unitMapping) → rates[], pullBookings(unitMapping) → bookings[], pushAvailability(unitMapping, blocks) → result, pushBooking(unitMapping, booking) → result. Implements 8 stub adapters (e.g., Guesty, Hostaway, Lodgify, Streamline, Escapia, BookingPal, NextPax, Rentals United) that return realistic mock data. Each adapter handles authentication stubs and data format translation.

sync_engine.name: Sync Orchestration Engine
sync_engine.description: Core sync logic: manages sync jobs (scheduled and on-demand), tracks sync state per unit+PMS (last_synced, sync_cursor, error_count), handles conflict resolution (last-write-wins with manual review queue for conflicts), rate limiting per PMS adapter, and retry with exponential backoff. Calls adapter pull methods, diffs against local state, applies changes to Availability/Pricing/Property services, and publishes sync events to Event Service. PostgreSQL stores sync state and conflict log.

sync_api.name: Sync API Endpoints
sync_api.description: Oak HTTP router implementing sync endpoints: POST /sync/trigger (trigger sync for unit/PMS), GET /sync/status/:unit_id (sync status per PMS), GET /sync/conflicts (list unresolved conflicts), POST /sync/conflicts/:id/resolve (resolve conflict with chosen version), GET /sync/adapters (list available PMS adapters and their status), PUT /sync/mappings (configure unit-to-PMS-unit mappings).

sync_tests.name: Sync Service Tests
sync_tests.description: Test suite for sync service: unit tests for each stub adapter (correct data format translation), sync engine conflict resolution tests, bidirectional sync flow tests (pull then push), rate limiting tests, API contract tests, error handling tests (adapter failure, partial sync), and integration tests verifying correct calls to Availability/Pricing services (mocked).

payments_service.name: Payments Service
payments_service.description: Stripe-mirrored payment processing with hash-chained payout snapshots for audit integrity. Manages payment intents, charges, refunds, and payouts. Mirrors Stripe objects locally for fast queries and audit trail. Payout snapshots are hash-chained (each snapshot includes hash of previous) creating a tamper-evident ledger. Uses mock Stripe client for testing.

payments_schema.name: Payments Database Schema & Repository
payments_schema.description: PostgreSQL schema and data access layer for payments. Tables: payment_intents (id, booking_id, stripe_intent_id, amount, currency, status, created_at), charges (id, payment_intent_id, stripe_charge_id, amount, status), refunds (id, charge_id, stripe_refund_id, amount, reason), payouts (id, property_id, amount, currency, status, period_start, period_end), payout_snapshots (id, payout_id, data JSONB, hash, prev_hash, created_at). Repository functions for all payment operations.

payments_stripe_mirror.name: Stripe Mirror Client
payments_stripe_mirror.description: Abstraction layer over Stripe API. In production, proxies to real Stripe; for tests, uses a mock Stripe that simulates payment intent creation, charge capture, refunds, and webhooks. Functions: createPaymentIntent(amount, currency, metadata) → intent, capturePayment(intentId) → charge, createRefund(chargeId, amount) → refund. Mirrors all Stripe objects to local DB after each operation. Handles pre-authorized payment tokens for the <3s checkout flow.

payments_hash_chain.name: Hash-Chained Payout Snapshots
payments_hash_chain.description: Implements tamper-evident payout ledger using hash chaining. Each payout snapshot contains: payout data, SHA-256 hash of (data + previous_hash), and reference to previous snapshot. Functions: createSnapshot(payoutId, data) → snapshot (auto-chains to previous), verifyChain(propertyId) → { valid: boolean, brokenAt?: snapshotId }, getChain(propertyId, since?) → snapshot[]. Genesis snapshot uses a well-known seed hash.

payments_api.name: Payments API Endpoints
payments_api.description: Oak HTTP router implementing payment endpoints: POST /payments/intents (create payment intent for booking), POST /payments/intents/:id/capture (capture authorized payment), POST /payments/refunds (create refund), GET /payments/bookings/:booking_id (payment history for booking), GET /payouts/:property_id (payout history), GET /payouts/:property_id/verify (verify hash chain integrity), POST /payouts (create payout with auto-snapshot).

payments_tests.name: Payments Service Tests
payments_tests.description: Test suite for payments: unit tests for hash chain integrity (verify chain, detect tampering, genesis snapshot), Stripe mirror tests with mock client (intent lifecycle, capture, refund), API contract tests, payout calculation tests, and edge cases (double capture prevention, partial refunds, chain fork detection).

booking_service.name: Booking Service
booking_service.description: Synchronous orchestrator for the complete booking flow, targeting <3s internal processing time. Coordinates calls to Availability (check+block), Pricing (quote), Property (unit details+settings), Payments (charge), and Event (publish booking events) services. Implements the saga pattern with compensating actions on failure (e.g., unblock dates if payment fails). This is the primary entry point for the checkout flow.

booking_schema.name: Booking Database Schema & Repository
booking_schema.description: PostgreSQL schema and data access layer for bookings. Tables: bookings (id, unit_id, guest_email, guest_name, check_in, check_out, guests, status enum [pending/confirmed/cancelled/completed], total_amount, currency, payment_intent_id, created_at, updated_at), booking_line_items (id, booking_id, description, amount, type). Repository functions for booking CRUD, status transitions with validation, and query by unit/date range/status.

booking_orchestrator.name: Booking Orchestration Engine
booking_orchestrator.description: Core booking flow orchestrator implementing the <3s checkout saga. Steps: 1) Validate input, 2) Check availability via Availability Service, 3) Get price quote via Pricing Service, 4) Get unit details via Property Service, 5) Create payment intent via Payments Service, 6) Block dates via Availability Service, 7) Capture payment via Payments Service, 8) Create booking record, 9) Publish booking.created event. Implements compensating actions: if step N fails, undo steps N-1...1 (unblock dates, cancel payment intent). Uses parallel calls where possible (steps 2+3+4 concurrently). Tracks saga state for recovery.

booking_api.name: Booking API Endpoints
booking_api.description: Oak HTTP router implementing booking endpoints: POST /bookings (full checkout flow — the 3-second endpoint), GET /bookings/:id (booking details), GET /bookings?unit_id=&status=&start=&end= (query bookings), POST /bookings/:id/cancel (cancel with refund orchestration), GET /bookings/:id/receipt (price breakdown and payment details). The POST /bookings endpoint is the critical path — it invokes the orchestrator and must return within 3 seconds of internal processing.

booking_tests.name: Booking Service Tests
booking_tests.description: Test suite for booking service: orchestrator happy-path test (all services succeed, booking created <3s), saga compensation tests (payment fails → dates unblocked, availability fails → no payment attempted), concurrent booking tests (two bookings for same dates — one wins), API contract tests, cancellation flow tests, and performance tests asserting orchestration overhead is <500ms excluding downstream service latency.
